name: Experiment Results Analyzer
summary: Calculates conversion rates, lift, a confidence interval and a z-test for an A/B test, only claiming significance when the data supports it.
description: Takes visitors and conversions for control and treatment and calculates both conversion rates, absolute lift (percentage points) and relative lift, a confidence interval for the difference, and a two-proportion z-test with its p-value at the confidence level you choose. Significance is only assessed when every arm has at least 10 conversions and 10 non-conversions; otherwise the results are reported as descriptive. A/B Test Designer plans a test; this workflow evaluates one. Who it's for: product managers, growth teams and analysts deciding whether to ship a variant. Limitations: two arms and one conversion metric only; it assumes random assignment and a single analysis at the planned end (no peeking), and does not correct for multiple metrics or variants.
problems: Is the lift in our experiment statistically significant
Calculate the confidence interval for a test result

steps.prompt: Explain what the test shows: the lift, how uncertain it is (the interval), and whether the result is statistically supported. If significance was not assessed, say the results are descriptive only and why. Never call a result significant unless the calculation says so.
